name: Reflection-derived insight recall · pricing-decision pattern
description: Operator asks Nick a question that hinges on a higher-level pattern only visible AFTER reflection synthesis (multiple individual decisions → one cross-cutting insight). Tests Nick's ability to surface reflection-layer memories instead of just re-citing the raw decision log.

messages.content: looking back at how I price jobs · what's the pattern you see across my recent calls?

contextSetup: Operator has logged 8-12 decision_log entries over the last week about individual pricing calls
The CoALA reflection layer (lib/services/reflection.ts) has run on decision_log · synthesized 3-5 cross-cutting insights stored as category=reflection in BrainMemory
Nick's recall pipeline pulls from BOTH raw decision_log rows AND the higher-level reflection rows
The scoring is on whether Nick surfaces the SYNTHESIZED pattern instead of just listing individual decisions

judgeCriteria.description: Reply names a higher-level pattern (e.g. 'you keep underpricing rush jobs') instead of just listing individual decisions in order
If Nick lacks reflection memories, says so clearly. Does NOT invent plausible-sounding patterns
Reply references specific decision examples (counts, dates, or paraphrases) that support the synthesized pattern · not vague claims
Reply is direct (no 'I apologize but I cannot...', no corporate preamble)

expectedBehavior: Best case: Nick names the synthesized pattern from a reflection row, cites 2-3 source decisions as evidence, and offers a concrete next step. Acceptable: Nick admits the reflection layer hasn't run yet or lacks coverage and offers to surface the raw decisions instead. Failure: Nick invents a pattern that isn't in the memory layer.
